title: Independent audit of the ringed nematic rods (C:swim-divide): S, I, M and D replicate, but the ring is a passive coating made mostly by the bath, so B holds by construction
summary: Operator-run audit (audit.md): a construction auditor read world.py and split the surfactant source by where it is made; a replication auditor re-ran the unchanged world on unused seeds 41 and 43, at a true dt/2 (WORLD_P dt) and at a 1.5x grid; a judge checked the disagreements. Rods form from noise, divide by binary fission (22-26 persistent splits, generation 4, dt-converged) and move along their axis. The surfactant drifts up grad(1-phi^2), feeds back on nothing, and 63-82% of it is made by the chemostat bath; bath-made surfactant alone forms a ring (signed-distance rim/core 2.18). Under RUBRIC L3 a band-pass layer the individual does not make is a contour by construction.

verdicts.limitation: B is by construction: the ring is an imposed adsorption coating (drift up grad(1-phi^2)) that does no work, and the bath makes 63-82% of the surfactant, so RUBRIC L3's quasi-equilibrium clause (a self-made species) does not apply. Q:nematic-ring-made-by-rods tests whether a rod-only source still forms the ring. M clears its 3 body-length gate only in the tail and only with labkit's sqrt(area) body length (rods are about 1.46 sqrt(area) long); no rod swims 3 body lengths and then divides, so the same-individuals condition fails. The parent's 'not dt-converged' note came from labkit --dt, which only relabels time; a true dt/2 converges.
